question: When is the Army Day celebrated in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**15 January.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Army Day in India is celebrated annually on **January 15th** to honor the soldiers and the Indian Army.
 
• This day marks the **taking over of the Indian Army by the first Indian Commander-in-Chief, Field Marshal K. M. Cariappa** from General Sir Francis Butcher in 1949.
 
• Various events, including parades and military shows, are organized at the **Army Command headquarters** to commemorate this occasion.
 
• The day is observed to acknowledge the **contributions and sacrifices of Indian soldiers** who guard the nation and ensure its security.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Field Marshal K. M. Cariappa**

 
 
• He was the first Indian Commander-in-Chief of the Indian Army.
 
• He took over the position from General Sir Francis Butcher on January 15, 1949.
 
• He is one of the only two Indian Army officers to hold the five-star rank of Field Marshal.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Army Day**
 
 
• It celebrates the valor, courage, and dedication of the Indian Army personnel.
 
• It is a day to pay homage to the martyrs who have laid down their lives for the country.
 
• The day also showcases the strength and capabilities of the Indian Army through various military displays and parades.
 
 
 
• **Indian Army**
 
 
• The Indian Army is the land-based branch and the largest component of the Indian Armed Forces.
 
• It is responsible for maintaining peace and security within the nation's borders and conducting operations during conflicts.
 
• The Indian Army also plays a crucial role in disaster relief and humanitarian assistance.
 
 
 
• **Military Parades**
 
 
• Military parades are an essential feature of Army Day celebrations.
 
• They include a display of various arms, equipment, and vehicles used by the Indian Army.
 
• Parades also feature a march-past by soldiers, showcasing their discipline and training.
